CSE - Link Error to Source Script.vi

Owning Palette: CSE Advanced VIs

The VI returns information on the statement of a parsed CSE script on which either a syntax error was met or a runtime error occurred.

Click the parameters for more information

 

get script source (T). If TRUE (by default), script indicator returns a source script of the specified parsed script.
CSE RefNum is a reference number for a CSE instance that contains a parsed CSE script. CSE - Parse Script.vi returns a value that can be wired directly to this terminal.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
script returns a source script of the specified parsed script if get script source control is equal to TRUE.
dup CSE RefNum is a flow-through parameter with the same value as CSE RefNum.
Stm Index returns an index of the statement on which either a syntax error was met or a runtime error occurred. If no error was encountered, it contains -1.
statement info returns information on a statement caused an error.
CE InstanceRef is a reference number of CalcExpress instance context that contains a parsed CalcExpress expression to evaluate. This value is only valid if stmType is equal to 0 (expression).
post action indicates a kind of jump-action to perform after the statement completes.

0jumpSet run position to jump index.
1jump if trueSet run position to jump index if expression is TRUE.
2jump if falseSet run position to jump index if expression is FALSE.
3stopfinish script execution.
jump index indicates an index of the next statement to perform. If post action indicates a conditional jump, jump index is effective if the condition is met during evaluation of the expression.
stmType indicates a type of the statement:

0expressionAn executable expression-statement to be evaluated.
statement info contains details on the statement location in a source script. The statement can be traced in a debugging mode.
1jumpAn executable jump-statement, which doesn't contain an expression (e.g. goto or break).
statement info contains details on the statement location in a source script. The statement can be traced in a debugging mode.
2source refNon-executable statement, which can be referred in an error message.
statement info contains details on the statement location in a source script. The statement can be traced in a debugging mode.
3jump stubAn executable jump-statement implicitly added by the parser. It cannot be referred in an error message.
This statement doesn't have direct link to a source script. It executes always but it cannot be traced in a debugging mode.
4source stubNon-executable statement, which can be referred in an error message.
statement info contains details on the statement location in a source script. It cannot be traced in a debugging mode. An example is an opening brace ( { ).
nesting level indicates a nesting level of the statement in structures like if, for, while. Zero value indicates the top level.
stmOffset contains an offset of the text-block in a source script associated with the statement.
stmLength contains length of the text-block in a source script associated with the statement.
stmLine contains a line number where the text-block in a source script associated with the statement begins. The first line has number one (1).
expOffset contains an offset of an expression in a source script if stmType is equal to 0 (expression). Otherwise, it is equal to -1.
expLength contains a length of an expression in a source script if stmType is equal to 0 (expression). Otherwise, it is equal to 0.
expLine contains a line number where an expression begins in a source script if stmType is equal to 0 (expression). Otherwise, it is equal to -1. The first line has number one (1).
parent index contains an index of the parent statement, or -1 if there is no a parent statement. This parameter is only applicable to expressions that are part of statements like if, for, while.
dup error in is a flow-through parameter with the same value as error in.
this VI error returns error information of this VI.
status indicates an error status.
code indicates either a CalcExpress error code or a LabVIEW error code if any occurred. If no error occurred, it is equal to zero.
source indicates the error description and information on this VI location if an error occurred.
Error Message returns an error description if either a syntax error was met or a runtime error occurred. It contains an empty string if no error was encountered.
